acceptance: make heavy-run CMD='echo $HOME' prints the home directory
A test or documented example covers a command containing a shell variable
description: Found 2026-11-11. `make heavy-run CMD='BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR=$HOME/Developer/benchmark_runs/x uv run -- benchbox run ... > $HOME/.../run.log 2>&1'` records and would run `BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR=OME/Developer/...`: make expands `$H` (empty) in the command-line variable before the recipe exports it. The lock record in `make heavy-status` showed the mangled command. The attempts here were refused by admission before running, so nothing was written, but an admitted run would have written benchmark output and the log to a relative `OME/` directory inside the checkout. make/tests.mk uses `$$CMD` in the recipe but does not protect the value. Other targets already use `override X := $(value X)` (make/pr-landing.mk) for this.
